headline: Underwriting profit widens as combined ratio improves
summary_short: Kinsale's second-quarter net income rose 31.1% year-over-year to $175.9 million as the combined ratio improved to 75.5% from 75.8%, even as gross written premiums fell 5.0% on continued Commercial Property competition. Diluted EPS was $7.72, up from $5.76 a year ago.
summary_long: Net income rose 31.1% y/y to $175.9M (diluted EPS $7.72, +34%) as underwriting income grew 10.5% to $105.4M and the combined ratio improved to 75.5% from 75.8%. The loss ratio fell to 53.8% from 55.1% on favorable prior-year reserve development; the expense ratio rose to 21.7% from 20.7% as higher reinsurance retention cut ceding commissions. Gross written premiums fell 5.0% to $527.6M on a 32.7% Commercial Property decline amid heightened competition; ex-Commercial Property, GWP grew 3.7%. Net investment income rose 19.9% to $55.7M. Cash fell to $210.5M after $100.9M of Q2 buybacks and $0.25/share dividends; the board expanded repurchase capacity to $337.5M in July. No forward guidance was issued.
